artists.biography:
One of New York’s most notable ska bands, the Slackers formed in Brooklyn in 1991 and have played the world over many times since. Their first release was an eponymous self-released album, distributed by Moon Records in 1993 on cassette. Their first real debut is “Better Late Than Never” on moon ska records. Coming out in 1996, this album saw a movement to more traditional ska music, as opposed to their earlier two-tone and garage influences. It was produced by Victor Rice, a noted ska/reggae producer, who also played bass for them at one point.

Band members are as follows:
Vic Ruggiero - Keyboards, Vocals
Jay “Agent Jay” Nugent - Guitar
Dave Hillyard - Saxophone
Glen Pine - Trombone, Vocals
Marcus Geard - Bass
Ara Babajian - Drums

perplexity.description:
Released in 1997 on Hellcat Records, Redlight is the second studio album by New York ska band The Slackers. The album is a defining work in their discography, showcasing their signature blend of ska, reggae, rocksteady, soul, jazz, and dub. Tracks like "Married Girl," "Watch This," and the title track "Redlight" highlight the band’s ability to merge upbeat rhythms with soulful melodies and introspective lyrics, establishing the eclectic sound that would become their hallmark.

Redlight solidified The Slackers’ reputation as one of the leading acts in the American ska and reggae scene. It received critical acclaim, ranking number seven on Billboard editor Carrie Bell’s “The Year in Music (1997)” list, and the title track charted on the CMJ Radio Top 200. The album’s enduring popularity is reflected in its status as a fan favorite, with many of its songs remaining staples in the band’s live sets. While later reissued by Pirates Press Records, the original 1997 release remains a landmark in the band’s career and a touchstone for fans of genre-blending reggae and ska.
